acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Wolves family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Dire Wolf, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Hamstring Pursuer archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Heavier chest and jaws, darker coarse coat, old flank scars, and a lower pursuit posture while remaining fully lupine.
Signature mechanic: Alternating Hamstring: only the Wolf on the prey's rear quarter attacks while its partner widens for the next exchange.
battlefieldDuty: Alternate pursuit with a packmate and slow isolated prey with a committed rear-leg bite.
constructionDimensions: Localized ember seams follow the chest, throat ruff, and working joints while heat-darkened guard hairs preserve the coat silhouette.
Directional smoke, sparking paw prints, and short flame tongues intensify only during lunges, howls, and pack signals.
counterplay: Break their angle with terrain or stagger the committed biter before the partner completes the swap. Affinity signal: The active shoulder or throat vent brightens through parted fur, then dims into a vulnerable cooling seam after commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: A wolf made entirely of featureless flame
Fire effects that hide pack direction or anatomy
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged lupine skeleton, long muzzle, visible paws, expressive ears, and a readable tail; no form becomes humanoid or wears manufactured armor.
Rank is communicated through chest mass, coat mantle, scars, posture, and pack behavior rather than arbitrary glow or simple scale.
Pack attack direction remains readable through gaze, ear position, tail line, paw placement, and the spacing of companion Wolves.
telegraph: Its head flattens beside the shoulder as the partner visibly widens formation.
